The '''Copa Chile''' (''Chile Cup'') is an annual cup competition for Chilean football teams. Due to time constraints and club pressure, the trophy was cancelled in 2000, but returned in 2008. Its precursor was the [[Campeonato de Apertura (Chile)|Campeonato de Apertura]] (''Opening Championship''), played from 1933 to 1950.

The cup is now open to every member club of the [[Chilean football league system]], from professional teams; ([[Primera División de Chile|Primera División]], [[Primera B (Chile)|Primera B]] & [[Segunda División de Chile|Segunda División]]), down to teams from the [[Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Amateur de Chile|ANFA]]: [[Tercera División de Chile|Tercera División]]. Since the season [[2009 Copa Chile|2009]], the winners obtained a direct [[Copa Sudamericana]] spot for the next season, however this was change starting from the [[2015 Copa Chile|2015]] edition; since then the winners obtains a direct [[Copa Libertadores]] spot for the next season.

In the history of the tournament, the [[Primera División de Chile|Primera División]] teams have dominated the competition; but, because this is contested in a knockout tournament format, the opportunity for lower-level teams upsetting a top level squad is a real possibility. That was the case in the seasons [[1960 Copa Preparación|1960]], [[1962 Copa Preparación|1962]], [[2009 Copa Chile|2009]] & [[2010 Copa Chile Bicentenario|2010]], when the winners were clubs from the [[Primera B (Chile)|second level]]: [[Deportes La Serena]], [[Luis Cruz Martínez de Curicó|Luis Cruz]], [[Unión San Felipe]] and [[Municipal Iquique]]. A major upset almost occurred in the [[2008 Copa Chile|2008 competition]], when [[Deportes Ovalle]] (from the [[Tercera División de Chile|third-level league]]) became finalist, losing 1–2 to [[C.D. Universidad de Concepción|Universidad de Concepción]] at the final, in a very close match.

In some seasons the tournament only included [[Primera División de Chile|first level]] teams, that was the case the seasons: 1979 to 1984, 1986, 1987, 1989-Invierno, 1990, 1998 and 2000.

Only two clubs have become [[Double (association football)|double champions]] (league and cup winners the same season); [[Colo-Colo]] in 1981, 1989, 1990 & 1996, and [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] in 2000.

==Trophy==
[[File:Copa Chile.png|thumb|upright|right|120px|Copa Chile trophy.]]
At the end of the final, the winning team is presented with a trophy, also known as the ''Copa Chile'', which they hold until the following year's final.  
 
The cup stands 120 centimetres tall and is made of 8&nbsp;kg of pure solid silver, its design includes the map of the Chilean territory (being four times around the trophy), made with stones of different colors, carved [[agate]], [[Onyx]] and [[lapis lazuli]].

The trophy was forged in 1974, in the ''Hernán Baeza Rebolledo workshop'', located in the commune of [[San Miguel, Chile|San Miguel]]. Its manufacture took nearly a month.

As well as winning the right to keep the trophy until the start of the next season, the winner gets to have a badge small silver plate at the pedestal of the trophy. The badge has the winners' name and the year of success.
